claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026.
Recovery teams led by the USS John P. Murtha secured the crew and capsule.
The splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean approximately 50 nautical miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
The U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha was stationed nearby to retrieve the four astronauts and the capsule.
The capsule performed a "skip entry" technique to manage heat and speed.
The capsule deployed drogue parachutes at 22,000 feet.
The capsule deployed main parachutes at 6,000 feet.
The crew underwent initial medical evaluations aboard the ship following recovery.
The crew returned to shore for transport to NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston.
